overview: Basman's 1...h6 against 1.Nf3 is a waiting move: Black prepares ...g5 or ...e5 and ...d5 with an odd kingside structure. White replies with a normal centre, e4 and d4 or c4 and g3, and gets a free hand. It is an offbeat choice seen mostly for surprise and does not give Black a concrete advantage.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with e4, d4 and c4 as Black has lost time
Develop normally and use the extra tempo
Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 if preferred

black_ideas.idea: Prepare ...g5 or ...e5 and ...d5 to claim the centre
Play ...e6 and ...d5 to reach a Dutch- or Queen's Pawn-like set-up
Surprise the opponent with unusual structures

typical_structures.structure: Flexible; ...h6 spends a tempo and Black structures vary

character.notes: Quiet and flexible without early tactics.

character.reason: Quiet and flexible; neither solid nor sharp.

soundness.reason: Wastes a tempo but not unsound.

level.reason: Few concrete lines but plans are vague.

plans.reason: No named plan from the evidence.
